Wen in a space suit at a starship window beside a card titled Fee rounding: thank you, fixed

Reader finding #1 from Wen Open Lab: Token-2022 rounds the transfer fee up, the lab's example rounded down (401 units gave a fee of 1, not 2), so the formula was fixed and two new tests were added. Status: fixed, 41 checks green.
Wen with a blue blade faces a figure with red blades beside a card: a memo exists is not the invoice is right

Reader finding #2: the Required Memo extension checks that a memo exists, not what it says, so a wrong invoice number still passes on-chain. The lab documented this known limit and added off-chain reconciliation with two tests.
Small Wen in a space suit under a giant glowing Wen spirit, card: two readers, two gaps, two fixes

Story card 1 of 5: a warranty card can live in your wallet and refuse to be resold
Did you know? Token-2022 has a NonTransferable token whose details live inside the mint, the same light NFT layout WNS uses. The base of the lab's warranty card model.
Story card 2 of 5: a payment can refuse to arrive without an invoice number
Did you know? Required memo, frozen-by-default accounts and a capped fee are built into the token itself, with no custom program. The base of the lab's B2B invoice model.
Story card 3 of 5: an NFT can carry its royalty rule inside the token
Did you know? A transfer hook runs on every transfer in every wallet; WNS uses it for creator royalties.
Story card 4 of 5: a small shop can match every payment to its order
Did you know? With Solana Pay each order gets one random reference key, then the shop validates the payment: no card number, no customer data.
Story card 5 of 5: all four models are open code, with a golden eye medallion
Did you know? Wen began as a poem split into a trillion tokens that grew into WNS, an open NFT standard on Token-2022. The four lab models are tested, devnet-ready and released under Apache-2.0.
